Check a module against a set of rules

Source: R/core-registry-contract.R
hr_check_module.Rd

Runs a module once and reports which of a list of rules it breaks. It is a report and nothing more: registering a module does not run it, and a module that breaks a rule is still registered and still runs. gr_check_reader() and gr_check_segmenter() use it with the rules for readers and segmenters.

Usage

hr_check_module(fn, run, rules = list(), kind = "module", name = NA_character_)

Arguments

fn

The module's function. The is_function rule checks that it is one.

run

A function of no arguments that calls the module once and returns what the rules are to check.

rules

A named list of rule functions, checked in order.

kind

The kind of module, such as "reader", for the report.

name

The module's name, for the report.

Value

An object of class hr_conformance: a data frame with one row per rule and the columns rule, ok (logical, NA for a rule that was not checked) and detail (character, "" when there is nothing to say). Its attributes are kind, name, contract (the contract version it was checked against) and warnings (the messages of the warnings the run raised). The first two rows are always is_function and runs. print() lists the broken rules first.

Details

run() is called with no arguments inside a temporary working directory, which is removed afterwards, so a module that writes files leaves nothing behind. An error it raises is caught and reported by the runs rule; its warnings are caught too, kept in the warnings attribute and not shown.

Each rule is a function of one argument, the value run() returned. It returns TRUE when the module passes, FALSE when it breaks the rule, and NA when the rule could not be checked on this run, or a list with ok (one of those three) and detail (one string saying why). A rule that raises an error is reported as broken, with the error as its detail. When run() fails, no rule is asked and each is reported as NA.

See also

gr_check_reader(), gr_check_segmenter()

Examples

double_it <- function(x) x * 2
hr_check_module(double_it, function() double_it(2),
  rules = list(numeric = function(v) is.numeric(v),
               above_three = function(v) list(ok = v > 3, detail = sprintf("got %s", v))),
  kind = "function", name = "double_it")
#> <hr_conformance> function 'double_it', contract 0.1
#>   passes all 4 rules
#>   ok    is_function
#>   ok    runs
#>   ok    numeric
#>   ok    above_three: got 4
